pr_title: Fix assert / ObjectDisposedException in PLINQ handling of AggregateException
pr_body:
PLINQ's QueryTaskGroupState handles joining with queued tasks, and handles the exceptions that emerge from waiting on them.  AggregateExceptions are special-cased, and are flattened to eliminate extra levels that may have been added explicitly or implicitly; the code then checks to see whether all of the exceptions contained in the aggregate represent cancellation.  However, it fails to account for the possibility that there are no exceptions it contains, which could happen if the only exceptions thrown are themselves empty AggregateExceptions.  If that happens, the code makes some invalid assumptions that lead to a failed assert and then throwing an ObjectDisposedException.

The fix is just to check whether the flattened AggregateException is empty and to treat that not as cancellation but as a normal exception.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/47710

Issue Details
### Description Being faced this unexpected behavior I found corresponding [thread on stackoverflow.com from 2013](https://stackoverflow.com/a/19392562/2336304) [Reproducing on .Net 5: https://dotnetfiddle.net/zT8Djq](https://dotnetfiddle.net/zT8Djq) ``` using System; using System.Linq; try { new int[10].AsParallel().Select(i => throw new AggregateException()).ForAll(Console.WriteLine); } catch (AggregateException) { Console.WriteLine("Expected"); } catch (ObjectDisposedException) { Console.WriteLine("Bug"); } ``` The code prints "Bug" when "Expected" expected. The problem is caused by QueryTaskGroupState.QueryEnd() implementation.
Author: Gladskih
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Linq`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

I can reproduce the issue in .NET 5. This seems to be a bug in the `ParallelEnumerable.ForAll` implementation when the source enumerable specifically throws `AggregateException`:
```csharp
static void Main()
{
    Repro<Exception>(); // works as expected
    Repro<DivideByZeroException>(); // works as expected
    Repro<AggregateException>(); // throws ObjectDisposedException

    static void Repro<TException>() where TException : Exception, new()
    {
        try
        {
            Enumerable.Range(0, 1).AsParallel().Select(i => (i > 0) ? i : throw new TException()).ForAll(_ => { });
        }
        catch (AggregateException)
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"Repro with {typeof(TException).Name} works as expected.");
        }
    }
}
```
The above fails with the exception:
```
Unhandled exception. System.ObjectDisposedException: The query enumerator has been disposed.
Object name: 'enumerator'.
   at System.Linq.Parallel.QueryTaskGroupState.QueryEnd(Boolean userInitiatedDispose)
   at System.Linq.Parallel.SpoolingTask.SpoolForAll[TInputOutput,TIgnoreKey](QueryTaskGroupState groupState, PartitionedStream`2 partitions, TaskScheduler taskScheduler)
   at System.Linq.Parallel.DefaultMergeHelper`2.System.Linq.Parallel.IMergeHelper<TInputOutput>.Execute()
   at System.Linq.Parallel.MergeExecutor`1.Execute()
   at System.Linq.Parallel.MergeExecutor`1.Execute[TKey](PartitionedStream`2 partitions, Boolean ignoreOutput, ParallelMergeOptions options, TaskScheduler taskScheduler, Boolean isOrdered, CancellationState cancellationState, Int32 queryId)
   at System.Linq.Parallel.PartitionedStreamMerger`1.Receive[TKey](PartitionedStream`2 partitionedStream)
   at System.Linq.Parallel.UnaryQueryOperator`2.UnaryQueryOperatorResults.ChildResultsRecipient.Receive[TKey](PartitionedStream`2 inputStream)
   at System.Linq.Parallel.UnaryQueryOperator`2.UnaryQueryOperatorResults.ChildResultsRecipient.Receive[TKey](PartitionedStream`2 inputStream)
   at System.Linq.Parallel.ScanQueryOperator`1.ScanEnumerableQueryOperatorResults.GivePartitionedStream(IPartitionedStreamRecipient`1 recipient)
   at System.Linq.Parallel.UnaryQueryOperator`2.UnaryQueryOperatorResults.GivePartitionedStream(IPartitionedStreamRecipient`1 recipient)
   at System.Linq.Parallel.UnaryQueryOperator`2.UnaryQueryOperatorResults.GivePartitionedStream(IPartitionedStreamRecipient`1 recipient)
   at System.Linq.Parallel.QueryOperator`1.GetOpenedEnumerator(Nullable`1 mergeOptions, Boolean suppressOrder, Boolean forEffect, QuerySettings querySettings)
   at System.Linq.Parallel.ForAllOperator`1.RunSynchronously()
   at System.Linq.ParallelEnumerable.ForAll[TSource](ParallelQuery`1 source, Action`1 action)
```

review_comments:
The bug for me reproduces with just one element, so might make sense to minimize the degree of parallelism.

```suggestion
            const int Count = 1;
```
It doesn't really matter, but I kept a value > 1 to highlight the case where multiple aggregate exceptions are boiled down to a single one.
If I changed the repro to throw an `AggregateException` populated with inner exceptions would the bug still reproduce?

> If I changed the repro to throw an AggregateException populated with inner exceptions would the bug still reproduce?

No (unless they were all themselves empty AggregateExceptions)
